```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Loading in libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```


```{r}
# Reading in data
clean <- read.csv("clean.csv")
head(clean)
```

```{r}
# Collecting general statistical summary
mean(clean$x1_month_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE)
median(clean$x1_month_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(clean$x1_month_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE)
min(clean$x1_month_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE)
max(clean$x1_month_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Reading in population dataset
pop <- read.csv("pop.csv")
head(pop)
```

```{r}
# Defining my states, filtering for the overlapping years
states_to_use <- c("Arizona", "Arkansas", "California", 
                   "Maine", "New Jersey", "Tennessee")

pop_sub <- pop |>
  filter(state %in% states_to_use,
         year %in% 2020:2025)

clean_sub <- clean %>%
  filter(state %in% states_to_use,
         year %in% 2020:2025)
```

```{r}
# Joining my datasets by state and year
merged <- pop_sub %>%
  inner_join(clean_sub, by = c("state", "year"))
```

```{r}
# Makes monthly averages into yearly average
unemp_yearly <- merged %>%
  group_by(state, year) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# Ensures correctly matching formats, filters down to years, then merges data
pop_sub$year <- as.integer(pop_sub$year)
unemp_yearly$year <- as.integer(unemp_yearly$year)
pop$year <- as.integer(pop$year)

final <- pop %>%
  filter(state %in% states_to_use,
         year %in% 2020:2025) %>%
  inner_join(unemp_yearly, by = c("state", "year"))
```

```{r}
# Distribution of population density 
hist(final$pop_density,
     main = "Population Density Distribution (2020–2025)",
     xlab = "Population Density (people per sq. mile)",
     ylab = "Frequency",
     col = "lightblue",
     border = "white")
```

```{r}
# Pearson correlation test
cor.test(final$pop_density, final$value, method = "pearson")
```

```{r}
# Looking at the correlation test per state
final %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(
    pearson  = cor(pop_density, value, method = "pearson"),
  )
# Only Cali is positive
# Driven by state differences, not trends :(
  # Denser state, higher unemployment- However, unemployment will fall while density is consistent
```

```{r}
# Scatterplot of results, with linear and loess plotted to compare the potential relationships
ggplot(final, aes(x = pop_density, y = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Population Density vs Unemployment",
       x = "Population Density",
       y = "Unemployment Rate")
```

```{r}
# Logarithmic transformation of the Pearson test
final$log_density <- log(final$pop_density)

cor.test(final$log_density, final$value)
  # Better
```
